results.ask: What's special about my block? I'm on 46th Ave between Moraga and Noriega.
results.expect: calls about_block; gives the block's own figures and something pinned nearby, with sources; cites
results.answer:
A few things stand out on 46th Ave between Moraga and Noriega:

- Your block sits about 39 feet above sea level, 0.2 miles from Ocean Beach, and most homes went up around 1941 — the tail end of the big Sunset building boom, just before wartime rules halted construction (SF Assessor's 2023 roll; USGS).
- Two blocks east, at 42nd and 43rd Ave between Moraga and Noriega, builders Henry Doelger and Ray Galli put up their named model homes: the Rainbow House (1941), Freedom House (1942), and The Challenger (1942) — among the last before the war stopped building (Western Neighborhoods Project; SF Planning's Sunset builders context statement).
- About 950 feet southwest, the Noriega seawall dates from the 1980s, and every year wind piles sand over it — in June 2023 Public Works moved about 30,000 cubic yards, waiting until the plovers had left (SF Public Works).
- A little farther down the beach, the clipper ship King Philip, wrecked in 1878, still lies buried under the sand near the foot of Noriega; her ribs surface after big winter storms (NPS).
- The OpenSFHistory archive has old photographs pinned near your block — two at 46th & Moraga, three at 45th & Noriega, and more along Noriega (Western Neighborhoods Project's archive).

Street cleaning: east side Monday 1st & 3rd, noon–2pm (next Nov 16); west side Thursday 1st, 3rd, 5th, noon–2pm (next Nov 19), per the city's sweeping schedule. The signs on the block are the last word.

If you know something about the block — who built your house, what the corner used to be — I'd be glad to add it to the notes for the next person who asks.
